newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite crude selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite crude selloff.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held relatively steady Thursday in quiet trade, but sinking crude, mild weather forecasts and cheap gas still left sentiment bearish, industry sources said.

"Gas is back, and with gas prices where they are, there's little or no demand," said one cash trader, noting a number of utilities had made the switch to natgas but mild East Coast weather had trimmed utility burns anyway.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged in the $16.50 a barrel area, with March one percent paper talked steady to down slightly at $16.20-45.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained quoted in the $17.25 area, but traders said softer city gate gas prices, now down to about $13.75 a barrel equivalent, were likely to keep HP on the defensive. Low pour was still in the low-to-mid $19s.
NYH high sulphurs also were steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged in the $15.25 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $15.25 and three percent at $13.00-25.
Traders said a major sold 60,000 barrels of USG prompt four percent (bunker quality) at $13.25.
New York city gate gas prices eased several cents to about $2.15/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid still at a $2.60/mmBtu equivalent.
